title: Fatal Attraction
author: Roger Auman
notes: The Caller's Box 10426, permission: full. The dance travels round the **major** set twice - 156 duple dances in the corpus do - and the promenade is what carries you to N2. A2's first two beats are the milestone's concurrency test: `(2) Women cast back || Men go forward`, two figures over disjoint dancers at the same beats, and they dance. "Men go forward" is a **dance-local figure** (D10). **The progression is carried by a figure in the middle of the dance** (M9b): A2's cast-back writes `"params": { "progresses": true }`, the clause `docs/dance-record.md` now documents, so the set's slots shift at the end of that call and everything after it resolves from one place along. The transcript's "N2 neighbor" is therefore written as `neighbors` from A2 on - the caller's own word is kept in each call's text - because after the shift the couple the promenade carried you round to **is** your neighbour. **Measured before and after, at every checked length (4-12):** reach went from **22.2982 px short** to **0.0000-2.6104 px**, which is the whole point - before the clause the dancer `N2` named was at every length a couple standing out, so A2's shoulder round, A2's swing and B1's promenade cast nobody at all and only A1's promenade travelled. `progressed` went from **68.0000 px** to **32.0000/37.7359 px**. Closure went the other way, from **18.8680-25.6125 px** to a uniform **37.7359 px**, and that is the one thing left. **The fill now writes back** (M9c): where a run of beats ends - at a call that carries the progression, or at a pass boundary - the couples that stood out for the whole of it have their `wait-out`'s own ends written into the set model, so the first call that sweeps them in starts them from where the crossing really left them. The beat-40 `walk-to-station -> allemande` seam is gone and **closure passes at 0.0000 px at four couples**, where it was 37.7359 at every length. **Still owed, and it is the dance's own shape rather than one seam.** Reach is **18.3771-26.7595 px short** (it was 0.0000-2.6104) and `progressed` is 40.0000-68.0000: telling the truth about where the waiting couple is standing exposes how far the dance then has to drag it. A becket couple that waits out the first eighteen beats crosses the set during them and comes in one couple place behind its new place, like every other body at a shift - and B1's allemande, written for the two robins by station, then reaches across that whole gap. Closure still fails at 29.9228 px (odd lengths) and 39.1798 (even), now at `robins-chain -> promenade`, beat 72 or 136. Collision is 0.000 px at every length. This dance is the one shape the engine has no mechanism for: **its progression is a figure in the middle of the time through, and which couples are standing out changes with it.** **One ruling the measurement did not support**, and it is recorded rather than taken: the clause was also measured with the shift applied to A1's promenade (closure 89-158 px, worse everywhere) and as a **model-only** shift that moves the relations without moving the seating (closure 5.77-52.50 px, reach 41-60 px short). The form committed - seating and relations together, at the cast-back - is the best of the three on reach by a factor of ten and is the one the milestone brief describes.

A1  (8) Ladies chain to neighbor  (8) Neighbor promenade counterclockwise around the major set
A2  (2) Women cast back || Men go forward  (6) N2 neighbor right shoulder round  (8) N2 neighbor swing
B1  (8) N2 neighbor promenade clockwise around the major set  (8) Women allemande right 1 & 1/2
B2  (4) Partner balance  (12) Partner swing

go-forward.describe: On your own, walk forward one place along the line you are standing in, still looking the way you were looking, while the dancer beside you casts back into the place behind them.

texts.description: One dancer walks forward one place along their own line.

walkthrough.line: Walk forward one place along your own line, looking the way you were looking.
walkthrough.teach: On your own, walk forward one place along the line you are standing in, still looking the way you were looking, while the dancer beside you casts back into the place behind them. Your hands stay at your sides: the two of you are dancing different figures in the same two beats.
